facts.f: Mohenjo-daro, an Indus Valley city, had a large public pool called the Great Bath.
facts.e: It was built more than 4,000 years ago with fired bricks and waterproofing.

facts.f: Emperor Ashoka turned to Buddhism and peace after the Kalinga War.
facts.e: He was saddened by the suffering of the war, and spread messages of kindness on rock edicts.

facts.f: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire, with the help of Chanakya.
facts.e: Chanakya is traditionally credited with writing the Arthashastra, a book on government.

facts.f: The Gupta period is often called a golden age of ancient India.
facts.e: Science, mathematics, art and literature flourished at that time.

facts.f: Gautama Buddha gained enlightenment under a tree at Bodh Gaya in Bihar.
facts.e: He gave his first sermon at Sarnath, near Varanasi.

facts.f: Mahavira was the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism.
facts.e: He taught non-violence (ahimsa) and truthfulness.

facts.f: Babur founded the Mughal Empire after winning the First Battle of Panipat in 1526.
facts.e: Mughal emperors ruled until 1857, though their power had shrunk greatly by then.

facts.f: The Mughal emperor Akbar welcomed scholars of many faiths to his court.
facts.e: His court had famous poets, scholars and musicians, including Birbal and Tansen.

facts.f: Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati of the Maratha kingdom at Raigad in 1674.
facts.e: He was known for his forts, his navy and his clever military tactics.

facts.f: The Battle of Plassey in 1757 helped the British East India Company gain power in Bengal.
facts.e: It was a big step towards British rule over India.

facts.f: The Revolt of 1857 is often called India's First War of Independence.
facts.e: Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi was one of its bravest leaders.

facts.f: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885.
facts.e: It became a leading organisation in India's freedom struggle.

facts.f: In 1930, Mahatma Gandhi led the Dandi March to protest against the British salt tax.
facts.e: He and his followers walked about 385 km from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi to make salt from seawater.

facts.f: The Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942.
facts.e: Gandhi gave the call 'Do or Die' to demand that the British leave India.

facts.f: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place in Amritsar on 13 April 1919.
facts.e: British troops fired on a peaceful crowd, which shocked India and the world.

facts.f: India and Pakistan became separate countries when British rule ended in August 1947.
facts.e: The Partition caused great suffering as millions of people had to move.

facts.f: Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of India's Constitution.
facts.e: He is often called the chief architect of the Constitution.

facts.f: India's Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949.
facts.e: It came into force on 26 January 1950. 26 November is celebrated as Constitution Day.

facts.f: Ancient Egyptians wrote using pictures and symbols called hieroglyphs.
facts.e: They wrote on papyrus, a kind of paper made from reeds.

facts.f: The Rosetta Stone helped scholars read Egyptian hieroglyphs.
facts.e: It has the same message in three scripts. Jean-François Champollion cracked the code in 1822.

facts.f: The ancient Olympic Games began in Olympia, Greece.
facts.e: By tradition, the first recorded games were held in 776 BCE.

facts.f: Julius Caesar was killed in Rome in 44 BCE, on the 'Ides of March'.
facts.e: The Ides of March was the 15th of March in the Roman calendar.

facts.f: Christopher Columbus reached the Americas in 1492.
facts.e: He was trying to find a sea route to Asia.

facts.f: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut (Kozhikode) in 1498.
facts.e: He was the first European to reach India by sailing around Africa.

facts.f: Ferdinand Magellan's expedition was the first to sail all the way around the world.
facts.e: It lasted from 1519 to 1522. Magellan himself died on the way.

facts.f: The French Revolution began in 1789.
facts.e: It spread the ideas of liberty, equality and fraternity.

facts.f: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the 1700s.
facts.e: Machines and factories began to replace hand-made goods.

facts.f: The United States declared independence from Britain on 4 July 1776.
facts.e: Americans celebrate 4 July as Independence Day.

facts.f: World War I lasted from 1914 to 1918. World War II lasted from 1939 to 1945.
facts.e: After World War II, the United Nations was set up to help keep peace.

facts.f: The Berlin Wall fell in 1989.
facts.e: Germany was reunited the next year, in 1990.

facts.f: Nelson Mandela became South Africa's first Black president in 1994.
facts.e: He had spent 27 years in prison for fighting against apartheid.

facts.f: Abraham Lincoln led the United States during its Civil War.
facts.e: His Emancipation Proclamation of 1863 was a major step towards ending slavery.

facts.f: Takshashila (Taxila) was one of the earliest centres of learning in the world.
facts.e: Students travelled long distances to study there.

facts.f: The Chola kings had a powerful navy.
facts.e: King Rajendra Chola I sent naval expeditions to South-East Asia.

facts.f: The Brihadeeswarar Temple in Thanjavur was built by Rajaraja Chola I.
facts.e: It was completed around 1010 CE and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

facts.f: Hampi in Karnataka was the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire.
facts.e: Its ruins of temples, markets and palaces are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

facts.f: Construction of the Qutub Minar in Delhi was begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak.
facts.e: It was completed by later rulers and is about 73 metres tall.

facts.f: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev were executed by the British on 23 March 1931.
facts.e: India remembers them on this day as Shaheed Diwas (Martyrs' Day).

facts.f: Subhas Chandra Bose led the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj).
facts.e: He is called 'Netaji'. He made the greeting 'Jai Hind' popular.

facts.f: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel helped join more than 500 princely states into India.
facts.e: He is called the 'Iron Man of India'.

facts.f: Mahatma Gandhi was born on 2 October 1869 in Porbandar, Gujarat.
facts.e: His birthday, Gandhi Jayanti, is also the International Day of Non-Violence.

facts.f: The Bhimbetka rock shelters in Madhya Pradesh have cave paintings thousands of years old.
facts.e: They show animals, hunting and dancing, painted by early humans.

facts.f: Paper was invented in China about 2,000 years ago.
facts.e: Tradition credits an official named Cai Lun with improving paper-making around 105 CE.

facts.f: The Magna Carta of 1215 limited the powers of the English king.
facts.e: It said that even the king had to follow the law.
